name: Higgs Boson Event Confidence Interval Estimation
description: The task involves estimating the signal strength (µ), representing the number of Higgs boson events normalized by the Standard Model prediction, and generating a 68.27% Confidence Interval (CI) for µ while accounting for systematic uncertainties.

cr:input.name: FAIR Universe HiggsML Dataset
cr:input.description: A tabular dataset of 280 million simulated proton-proton collision events, with 28 features per event. Features include primary attributes (e.g., energy and momentum of particles) and derived attributes calculated using domain-specific knowledge. Each event is labeled as either a Higgs boson event or a background event. The dataset includes systematic bias parameterizations and is stored in Parquet format.
cr:input.contentUrl: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset download URL]

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: The output consists of a 68.27% Confidence Interval (CI) for the signal strength µ. The CI is represented by two bounds: µ16 (lower bound) and µ84 (upper bound). Example: µ16 = 0.8, µ84 = 1.2.

field.name: mu16
field.description: Lower bound of the 68.27% Confidence Interval for the signal strength µ. Example: 0.8.

field.name: mu84
field.description: Upper bound of the 68.27% Confidence Interval for the signal strength µ. Example: 1.2.

cr:evaluation.notes: Quantile Score is computed as -ln((w + ϵ)f(c)), where w is the average CI width, c is the coverage, and f(c) is a penalizing function for deviations from 68.27% coverage. Overestimating uncertainty incurs a smaller penalty than underestimating it.
